_comment: WORK slider -> project detail pages. project.html?p=<slug> reads this file and renders one entry. 'hero'/'media' items are {src, kind, caption} — kind is 'image' (default) or 'video'; missing/null src falls back to the halftone placeholder, same convention as the gallery. 'media' items may set 'full': true to span the full width instead of sitting in the 2-up grid. 'credits' is a flat label/value list.

projects.title: Night Shift
projects.headline: Handheld takes from a single night, cut to the sound of the room.
body: We shot on a single permit, one night, no second unit. The brief was simple: nothing that couldn't have happened if the camera weren't there. Available light, a rain machine for one scene, and a crew small enough to fit in the frame without meaning to.
The edit keeps every wobble and every dead second between takes that mattered. The grade is muted on purpose — Prague after midnight reads better slightly underexposed than corrected into daylight.

projects.title: Snake Height
projects.headline: A logotype pulled apart until the counters break, then printed badly on purpose.
body: The brand asked for something that could survive a bad print run better than a good one. We built the mark from a single continuous stroke, then let it distort under pressure — literally, by running early proofs through a broken riso drum until the registration slipped in a way worth keeping.
The final system keeps that slip as a rule, not an accident: every application carries a small, deliberate misalignment. It reads as handmade at any size, from a business card to a hoarding.

projects.title: Halftone Atlas
projects.headline: A hundred plates at increasing dot density — the point is the moment it stops reading.
body: Same photograph, printed a hundred times, each pass pushed further into the halftone grid until the image gives up and becomes pure pattern. It's less a print run than a stress test for how much information an audience actually needs to recognise a face.
Bound as a small run of hand-numbered atlases, riso-printed two colours at a time. No two copies register quite the same way.

projects.title: S*burban
projects.headline: A fashion film shot on the edge of the city, mostly at dusk.
body: We scouted the last blocks before the ring road gives up and becomes field — half-built facades, empty forecourts, the kind of light that only lasts twenty minutes. The collection was built around movement, so we shot it running, mostly handheld, mostly against the clock.
No studio, no lighting rig bigger than what fit in a hatchback. What's on screen is what golden hour actually gave us that evening, graded to hold onto it a little longer than it lasted.

projects.title: Legacy Project
projects.headline: A campaign built entirely from archive material and a scanner.
body: No new photography. The brief was to make forty years of filed-away contact sheets, slides and internal memos feel like a present-tense campaign rather than a retrospective — so everything you see was scanned flatbed, at full grain, off whatever the client's basement actually held.
Layout follows the logic of a contact sheet rather than a moodboard: nothing cropped, nothing retouched, sequence numbers left visible on purpose.

projects.title: Raw Archive
projects.headline: An index that refuses to explain itself — scroll is the only interface.
body: No menu, no filters, no captions. Everything the studio has ever shot lives on one continuously scrolling page, ordered by nothing more meaningful than when it was uploaded. Finding something specific is not really the point.
Built as a way to keep raw footage circulating instead of sitting on a drive — a living contact sheet that grows every time something new gets shot.
